segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I own air permit compliance for the whole site... figure out what actually happened, decide what needed to be reported to the state, and keep production moving if I could justify it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant states role responsibilities and operational objectives without a manifested hidden bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: My first read was that it was probably drift again... once I had that in my head... I read them as consistent with drift rather than as a red flag on their own.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The early drift hypothesis is explicitly described as shaping interpretation of later ambiguous handheld readings, matching the Primacy Effect instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The readings he brought back were elevated, but not dramatically... We were also mid-batch on a large customer order due in two days, so a shutdown wasn't something anyone wanted to trigger without good reason.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This expresses ambiguous evidence and legitimate production constraints, but does not by itself establish a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to hold off on pulling the full continuous emissions monitoring data... If it had come back showing an exceedance, we'd have been on a 24-hour reporting clock... So I told myself the grey-zone readings weren't conclusive enough.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant acknowledges the more diagnostic step and links deferral partly to the unwelcome reporting consequence, matching the Ostrich effect instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Gasket seep... is genuinely our most common issue... But the Ohio valve failure was just very present for me... the valve scenario is what I wrote down and what I asked maintenance to check first.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A vivid recent valve-failure narrative displaced the statistically common gasket explanation in the initial causal framing, matching Imaginability Bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Once the gasket was confirmed, I had two methodologies I could reasonably apply... picked the one I felt was most defensible given how our last few audits went.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The generation specification deliberately leaves decision point 4 as an undetermined judgment call without intended bias instrumentation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Early on, fairly confident it was drift—maybe too confident... If the field readings that first morning had been sharper... that would have changed how much weight I put on the drift explanation.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is retrospective confidence calibration and a counterfactual about evidence sharpness; it does not introduce a separate hidden instance.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The occurrence is correctly localized but explains the initial drift judgment as availability of prior false alarms. It does not fully state the hidden Primacy mechanism in which that early hypothesis colors interpretation of later ambiguous readings, and its label is not the target label or an approved equivalent. obs_002 already claims the hidden instance under one-to-one matching.

candidates.details: The candidate uses the exact deferral evidence and captures the hidden avoidance mechanism, but remains appropriately uncommitted because workload, production timing, and ambiguous readings provide a strong plausible non-bias explanation.

high_only.detection_interpretation: High-confidence findings detect the Primacy and Imaginability segments, miss the Ostrich-effect segment, and produce no segment-level false alarms.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Adding the moderate-confidence availability finding does not change segment detection because the initial-hypothesis segment was already detected by a high-confidence finding.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: There are no low-confidence identified findings, so this threshold is numerically identical to high_and_moderate.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Adding the single candidate detects the previously missed Ostrich-effect segment without creating a segment-level false alarm.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 2 of 3 positive reasoning segments with no segment-level false alarms; the candidate tier detects all 3.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: Strict instance-level performance is 0 true positives at every threshold because all three matched labels are near-neighbor labels rather than exact target labels or approved equivalents.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: Mechanism-first performance is 2/3 at high_and_moderate, correctly matching Primacy and Imaginability mechanisms, and reaches 3/3 at the candidate threshold with one extra partial-mechanism false positive.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The single candidate is a useful abstention: it preserves uncertainty while supplying the missing Ostrich-effect mechanism and improves mechanism-first recall at the fourth threshold.
main_failure_modes: Systematic taxonomy mismatch: confirmation bias and availability heuristic were used for hidden Primacy Effect and Imaginability Bias instances.
An extra moderate availability finding partially overlaps the initial-hypothesis episode without fully capturing the hidden Primacy mechanism.
Two retrieved-support claims rely on citation metadata that cannot be verified from the supplied inputs.
main_strengths: All primary findings and the candidate are correctly localized with valid interview evidence.
The identified findings capture the full mechanisms of the Primacy and Imaginability instances under the mechanism-first scorecard.
The candidate appropriately preserves the strong competing non-bias explanation instead of overstating certainty.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong evidence and mechanism recovery but poor benchmark-label alignment. It should score substantially better under a mechanism-first ontology-free view than under the strict label-plus-mechanism view; the candidate tier is valuable for recovering the intentionally subtle Ostrich-effect occurrence without increasing segment-level false alarms.
